references.text: Describes the plagues and oppression that the Egyptians inflicted on Israel, as Moses told his father-in-law.
The first plague against Egypt - water turned to blood. Part of what the Lord did to Pharaoh and Egypt.
The Lord's deliverance of Israel at the Red Sea, where he rescued them from the Egyptians.
The song of Moses and Israel summarizing what the Lord did to Pharaoh and Egypt.
The attack by the Amalekites on Israel along the way - one of the hardships (תְּלָאָה) they encountered on the journey.
Moses sends a message to the king of Edom and summarizes all the similar hardships Israel faced.
A confession summarizing Israel's sufferings in Egypt and the Lord's deliverance.
The Levites' prayer recounting everything the Lord did to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, and how he delivered Israel.
The psalm recounts the Lord's signs in Egypt and his deliverance of Israel.
Summary of the plagues the Lord sent upon Egypt for Israel's sake.
Describes the Lord's miracles in Egypt and at the Red Sea.
Stephen's speech referring to Moses, who led the people out after performing wonders and signs in Egypt.
The verses describe the same sequence of events: first Jethro receives the news (v.1), then Moses shares the details with him (v.8).
Both verses use the memory of the exodus from Egypt as a foundation for the relationship with God, even though the audience and occasion differ.
